observations.statement: The staged contract documents POST /api/v2/disaster/spending_by_geography/ with required body keys filter, geo_layer, and spending_type, plus optional geo_layer_filters and scope.
The filter object documentation explicitly includes required filter.def_codes and optional filter.award_type_codes.
The documented response echoes geo_layer, scope, and spending_type and returns results rows with shape_code, amount, display_name, population, per_capita, and award_count.
The staged markdown contains an internal mismatch: the Schema block labels the POST body as type string while the attributes and example body clearly describe a JSON object payload.

source.title: Retired low-level artifact for disaster spending_by_geography

observations.statement: The retired low-level artifact treats the request body as an object and preserves nested filter fields filter.time_period, filter.recipient_scope, and filter.recipient_locations in addition to documented filter.def_codes and filter.award_type_codes.
The retired low-level artifact says scope defaults to recipient_location when omitted and notes geo_layer_filters act as an allowlist of shape codes for the chosen geography layer.

The retired low-level artifact reports that results may include a null shape_code/display_name aggregate bucket when uncoded spending cannot be assigned to a geography, especially when geo_layer_filters are omitted.
The retired low-level artifact includes both 400-style enum validation and 422-style minimum-items validation in examples, so callers should expect multiple validation status families.

source.title: Derived retired MCP coverage check for disaster spending_by_geography

observations.statement: The semantic endpoint-facing MCP surface exposes the top-level body keys filter, geo_layer, geo_layer_filters, scope, and spending_type, but coding agents still need nested filter paths such as filter.def_codes and shared search keys to build useful requests.
Because the endpoint is an aggregate geography surface with no paging or award identifiers, downstream drill-down usually requires a second endpoint keyed by the same DEFC and geography filters.

source.title: Live USAspending probes for disaster spending_by_geography on 2026-05-10

observations.statement: A minimal DEFC L state obligation request returned HTTP 200, confirming the route is live and that omitting scope defaults the response to recipient_location.
The live response included a row with null shape_code and null display_name, confirming an uncoded aggregate bucket that contradicts the documentation's required-string description for those fields.
The baseline state response included both positive and negative amounts; New Jersey appeared with a negative obligation total.

source.title: USAspending award search and shared search filter docs for state drilldown mapping

observations.statement: The spending_by_award search docs support def_codes alongside recipient_scope plus recipient_locations and place_of_performance_scope plus place_of_performance_locations, so disaster DEFC filters can be preserved while drilling from geography aggregates into award-level search.

The shared search-filter docs show state-level location objects formatted like {"country":"USA","state":"VA"}, which makes non-null disaster geography state shape_code values directly reusable as downstream award-search state filters.

The staged DEFC reference documents GET /api/v2/references/def_codes/ as a lookup that returns each code with its public_law, title, urls, and disaster grouping, giving callers a path to translate raw def_codes into plain-language labels.
In that staged DEFC reference, code L is documented as Emergency P.L. 116-123 with title Coronavirus Preparedness and Response Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2020 and disaster group covid_19.

source.title: Live USAspending probes for disaster spending_by_geography on 2026-05-15

observations.statement: A request containing filter.time_period, recipient_scope=domestic, and recipient_locations=[{"country":"USA","state":"CA"}] returned HTTP 200, confirming the endpoint parser accepted those shared passthrough keys in this probe.

Despite those extra shared filters, the response still returned 60 rows and the same leading DEFC L state amounts and ordering pattern seen in the unbounded baseline, indicating the supplied time_period and recipient-location filters did not materially narrow the geography rollup in this run.
The returned order was not descending by amount: California appeared before larger Maryland, Virginia, District of Columbia, and Massachusetts rows.

The reviewer report states that endpoint facts already mark geo_layer=state as the strongest live-verified path while geo_layer=county and geo_layer=district remain documented but not re-probed in this bundle, and that validateRequest should emit caller-visible warnings rather than silently treating those layers as equally verified.

The same reviewer report states that spending_type=face_value_of_loan remains documented but not re-probed in this bundle and should likewise trigger a caller-visible validation warning while remaining transport-valid.

The reviewer report says the promoted semantic MCP surface available in this run did not expose a promoted semantic DEFC translation endpoint or tool, even though this geography bundle's workflow told callers to translate DEFC codes before storytelling.

The reviewer report documents that story_list_mcp_tools showed no promoted usaspending.v2__references__def_codes tool and a follow-up semantic discovery search for DEFC references did not surface a promoted semantic DEFC translation endpoint.
Until semantic promotion exists, any instruction to use GET /api/v2/references/def_codes/ should be labeled as an external raw fallback rather than implied as an in-surface semantic step.
